findings.title: GitHub contribution activity (12 months)
findings.evidence: GitHub reports 33,586 contribution-calendar events in the last 12 months (15,671 commits, 4,190 pull requests, 219 reviews, and 2,504 issues)
findings.analysis: This is an activity count, not a count of shipped units. GitHub events vary in scope and do not establish review, merge, quality, or impact.

findings.title: Visible organization memberships
findings.evidence: GitHub returned 10 organization memberships for this account
findings.source: GitHub GraphQL user.organizations (first 20 visible to the token)
findings.analysis: Membership does not by itself establish ownership, administrative authority, or individual responsibility for every repository in an organization.

findings.title: Pull requests opened (12 months)
findings.evidence: GitHub reports 4,190 pull requests opened in the trailing 12-month collection
findings.analysis: Opened pull requests are activity events; this field does not say whether they were reviewed, mergeable, merged, distinct in scope, or created without automation.

findings.title: Visible non-fork repository corpus
findings.evidence: 290 non-fork repositories were visible across the personal account and 10 organization memberships returned by the API
findings.source: GitHub GraphQL repositories connections with isFork=false
findings.analysis: Organization repositories can include work by other contributors. Visibility does not establish individual authorship, maintenance, or operation.

findings.title: Account age
findings.evidence: The GitHub account was created in 2016 (9.6 years ago)
findings.analysis: Account age is not equivalent to continuous professional experience or activity.

findings.title: Primary-language breadth of the visible corpus
findings.evidence: GitHub assigns 17 distinct primary-language labels across the visible non-fork corpus — led by Python (109), TypeScript (50), HTML (24), JavaScript (21), Shell (15)
findings.source: Distinct repository.primaryLanguage.name values in the visible corpus
findings.analysis: A repository has one GitHub-assigned primary language. This describes the corpus and does not establish individual proficiency or authorship.

findings.title: Mapped language-layer coverage
findings.evidence: The static language map places the visible corpus in 5 layers: backend, creative, frontend, infra, native
findings.analysis: This is a corpus classification, not evidence that one person authored, shipped, or is proficient in every mapped layer.
